Mise à jour du 29 octobre 2026 : -75 % et pivot vers le foie

  • 345 → 87 pubs actives en 2 jours (-75 %) : Black Seed 140 → 40, Purely-Nutrient 83 → 31, Top 10 Holistic Tips 44 → 4, The Ethiopian Journal 61 → 5. La marque sort des 7 classements (elle était 1re sur « Flomax » le 27 octobre).
  • 22 nouvelles vidéos du 24 octobre, presque toutes sur le foie gras (fatty liver = foie engraissé) : « This is what happens when milk thistle hits your fatty liver versus when thymoquinone does » (4 variantes, voir), « Watch what happens when you put a fatty liver in contact with apple cider vinegar… Now watch… thymoquinone at 4.64 percent » (3 variantes, voir).
  • Une seule reste prostate, même mécanique : « Watch what happens when you put a swollen prostate in contact with Flomax. The swelling reduces slightly… but the urethra remains compressed. Now watch what happens when that same prostate tissue comes in contact with thymoquinone at 4.64 percent » (3 variantes, voir).
  • Lecture : les 345 pubs prostate ne tenaient pas ; ils gardent la formule « Watch what happens » (comparaison ingrédient classique contre thymoquinone, dose précise 4,64 %) et changent d'organe. À resurveiller dans 2 relevés : si le foie remonte à 300+, c'est que la mécanique marche mieux que le sujet prostate.

En une phrase

Purely Nutrient vend de l'huile de nigelle éthiopienne (black seed oil), est passé de 0 à 365 pubs actives en un mois (lancement mi-septembre 2026) sur 5 pages, et occupe la 1re place sur « enlarged prostate » et les places 1-2-3 sur « Flomax » alors que le texte de ses pubs ne parle même pas de prostate : tout se joue dans la vidéo et le ciblage.

Angles marketing (57 pubs lues, 55 vidéos)

  • Un seul texte de pub, répété 46 fois : « Purely Nutrient Ethiopian Black Seed Oil is one of nature's most potent, time-tested remedy. Sourced exclusively from Ethiopia's volcanic highlands… Cold-pressed… third-party tested… softgels ». Le texte est neutre ; c'est la vidéo qui porte l'angle (voir transcriptions ci-dessous).
  • Thymoquinone 5 × : « Regular black seed oil has 0.5%–1% thymoquinone. Ethiopian black seed oil has up to 4.64%… 5× more potent, grown at 8,000 ft ». Argument de pureté/origine (comme la Styrie chez Elivora).
  • Parasites, biofilms, Toxoplasma : « the compound that dissolves parasite shells, fungal biofilms, and bad bacteria », « It's called Toxoplasma. It forms microscopic cysts inside your brain… 1 in every 3 humans », « In February Ellie had pinworms ». Angle « il y a quelque chose en vous » très viral en 2026 (tendance « parasite cleanse »).
  • Remède ancestral : « time-tested remedy », « generations of cultivation » : la nigelle comme remède millénaire (Égypte, prophète).
  • Version espagnole de la même pub (« es uno de los remedios naturales más potentes ») : ils testent le marché hispanique US.

Cible

  • Large : hommes et femmes de plus de 40 ans, « wellness » généraliste (brouillard mental, énergie, digestion, inflammation).
  • Via le ciblage et les vidéos : hommes de plus de 50 ans avec prostate gonflée / sous Flomax (sinon ils ne seraient pas 1er sur ces recherches).
  • Grands-parents (histoire de la petite-fille et des oxyures) : cible 55-70 ans qui partage sur Facebook.
  • Hispanophones US (pubs en espagnol).

Promesses

  • « Brain fog lifts », énergie, digestion, inflammation en baisse ; « dissolves parasite shells ».
  • Pour la prostate (dans les vidéos) : moins d'inflammation, moins de levers la nuit.
  • Pureté : cold-pressed, testé par un tiers, « zero unnecessary » additifs.

Offres et pages de vente

  • purelynutrient.com/pages/ethiopian-black-seed-oil (46 pubs) : page de vente unique, longue, type « listicle ».
  • purelynutrient.com/pages/pp-48 (11 pubs) : variante de page (test).
  • 5 pages Facebook : « Purely Nutrient Black Seed », « Purely-Nutrient », « The Ethiopian Journal », « Top 10 Holistic Tips », « The Wellness Journal » : des pages « média » (journal, top 10) pour que la pub ressemble à un article.

Formats

  • Vidéo à 96 % (55 sur 57) : le même texte, des dizaines de vidéos différentes (c'est le contraire d'Elivora). Ils testent la créa vidéo en masse avec un texte fixe.
  • Texte court, pas de récit long : la vidéo fait le travail.
  • Page « Top 10 Holistic Tips » = leur meilleure page en classement (1re sur « enlarged prostate » et « Flomax »).

Ce que disent les vidéos (6 transcrites sur 55) : c'est LÀ qu'est l'angle prostate

  • « This is a swollen prostate » (16 sept 2026, 3 variantes, 5 000 car. de script) : répété trois fois en ouverture, puis « three warning signs » : jet faible (« a fist around a garden hose »), levers la nuit, fuite après avoir remis le slip. Mécanisme vendu : « chronic inflammation… like cement, hardened waste, toxins, and hormonal byproducts compounding inside the tissue year after year ». Menace : « a scope up your urethra… surgery with a 75% chance of permanent side effects ».
  • « This is a dead prostate » (3 variantes) : « the best thing to fix it is not saw palmetto, pumpkin seeds, or the medication your urologist keeps pushing » : ils attaquent directement la courge et le saw palmetto (donc Everly, Elivora et Uromend) pour vendre la nigelle.
  • Le voyage de 72 heures (2 vidéos, prostate et intestin) : « You accidentally swallow a softgel of Ethiopian black seed oil. It can still affect your prostate for the next 72 hours… By hour 12, the thymoquinone passes directly through the cell membranes of your prostate tissue… By hour 24… the tissue begins to soften… By hour 48… ». Format « que se passe-t-il dans votre corps heure par heure », très regardé.
  • Sexe + Flomax (3 variantes) : « This is how a 42-year-old man gets his big loads back without ever touching another Flomax refill… The dry orgasms. The cloudy dribble after… every Flomax refill just relaxed the pipe while the swelling sat there getting worse ». Même structure « 3 jours / jour 10 / 3 semaines » que Noverly (même rédacteur ou même modèle).
  • Parasites / candida (femmes) : « Clean your vagina in just one night… there's something alive inside you… parasites build a thick protective shield called biofilm. Wormwood bounces right off it ». Le mot biofilm revient partout : c'est leur mécanisme signature (« dissolves that biofilm »).
  • Preuve : « tested at 4.64% thymoquinone. Nine times stronger » ; « Highland farms at 8,000 feet ».
  • Les deux vidéos « prostate » sont celles qui portent 3 variantes chacune : ce sont leurs meilleures. Elles sont téléchargeables depuis la fiche (copie locale gardée).

Hooks, niveau de conscience, personas, ennemis, narratif (chiffres indicatifs du 17/10 ; les graphes en dessous sont recalculés à chaque relevé)

  • Hook texte n°1 : le catalogue (93 % : le même texte « Purely Nutrient Ethiopian Black Seed Oil is one of nature's most potent… ») : le vrai hook est dans la vidéo : « This is a swollen prostate » (×3), « This is a dead prostate » (×3), « You accidentally swallow a softgel… 72 hours », « Clean your vagina in just one night ».
  • Niveau de conscience : le texte parle au conscient du produit (91 % : le nom de la marque dès la première ligne) ; les vidéos, elles, parlent à l'inconscient (« il y a quelque chose en vous : parasites, hardened waste ») et au conscient du problème (prostate).
  • Persona (d'après les vidéos transcrites) : homme 50+ prostate (les 2 meilleures vidéos), femme 40+ (candida, parasites), grands-parents (oxyures), hispanophones.
  • Ennemi : les parasites / le biofilm / les déchets durcis (leur mécanisme signature), les autres compléments (« not saw palmetto, pumpkin seeds »), le Flomax (« every Flomax refill just relaxed the pipe »).
  • Narratif : catalogue (texte) + mécanisme chronologique en vidéo (72 h, jour 3/10, 3 semaines) + image choc répétée trois fois.

Ce que ça veut dire pour Uromend

  • La nigelle arrive sur le terrain prostate (Sabel Life aussi) : c'est un ingrédient à la mode ; Uromend n'en a pas. Pas besoin d'en mettre, mais prévoir la question « et la black seed oil ? » dans les pubs/FAQ.
  • Leur méthode (texte fixe + 50 vidéos) est l'inverse d'Everly/Elivora (image + 50 textes). Uromend fait peu des deux. La méthode Purely est la plus accessible pour Saad (montage vidéo) : garder un texte qui marche et produire 5 vidéos par semaine.
  • Être 1er sur « enlarged prostate » en un mois avec un produit non prostate montre que la place se gagne avec le volume et le ciblage, pas avec la pertinence : Uromend peut la reprendre avec 30-50 vidéos sur le même angle.
  • Les pages « journal / top 10 » (média déguisé) sont une idée propre à reprendre : une page « Men's Night Guide » ou « Prostate Health Daily » qui publie des conseils et des pubs.
  • À surveiller : 0 → 365 en un mois ; si le prochain comptage montre 600+, ils ont trouvé une vidéo gagnante : la transcrire et l'analyser en priorité.

  • 87 → 302 pubs actives (+247 %), après 345 → 87 le relevé d'avant : The Ethiopian Journal 5 → 62, Top 10 Holistic Tips 4 → 46, The Wellness Journal 6 → 42, Purely Nutrient Black Seed 40 → 81, Purely-Nutrient 31 → 69. Lancées presque toutes le 30 octobre.
  • La prostate se cache dans les vidéos : sur 89 pubs récoltées, le texte ne cite jamais « prostate » ni « Flomax » (54 citent le foie, « liver »). Mais 3 hooks vidéo sur les 5 transcrits parlent de prostate : « Here's how to take black seed oil for your prostate the right way… I'm a urologist » (voir), « Watch what happens when you put a swollen prostate in contact with Flomax » (voir), et une offre « buy two, get one free » (voir). Ce n'est donc pas un abandon de la prostate.
  • Espagnol en force : 29 pubs sur 89 sont en espagnol. Nouvelles histoires longues hors santé masculine : genoux (« bone on bone »), tension (« Stalin's Doctors »), couple (« He's 61. I'm 32 »).
  • Pages de vente : ethiopian-black-seed-oil (58 pubs), pp-48 (29 pubs).

  • Pour Uromend : ce yo-yo montre qu'une chute sur un seul relevé ne veut rien dire chez eux. L'espagnol reste un terrain peu pris sur la prostate (à tester).

In one sentence

Purely Nutrient sells Ethiopian black seed oil, went from 0 to 365 active ads in one month (launched mid-September 2026) across 5 pages, and holds #1 on "enlarged prostate" and #1-2-3 on "Flomax" even though its ad copy doesn't even mention the prostate: everything happens in the video and the targeting.

Marketing angles (57 ads read, 55 videos)

  • One ad copy, repeated 46 times: "Purely Nutrient Ethiopian Black Seed Oil is one of nature's most potent, time-tested remedy. Sourced exclusively from Ethiopia's volcanic highlands… Cold-pressed… third-party tested… softgels". The copy is neutral; the video carries the angle (see transcripts below).
  • Thymoquinone 5×: "Regular black seed oil has 0.5%–1% thymoquinone. Ethiopian black seed oil has up to 4.64%… 5× more potent, grown at 8,000 ft". A purity/origin argument (like Styria for Elivora).
  • Parasites, biofilms, Toxoplasma: "the compound that dissolves parasite shells, fungal biofilms, and bad bacteria", "It's called Toxoplasma. It forms microscopic cysts inside your brain… 1 in every 3 humans", "In February Ellie had pinworms". The "something is living inside you" angle, very viral in 2026 (the "parasite cleanse" trend).
  • Ancient remedy: "time-tested remedy", "generations of cultivation": black seed as a thousand-year-old remedy (Egypt, the Prophet).
  • Spanish version of the same ad ("es uno de los remedios naturales más potentes"): they are testing the US Hispanic market.

Target

  • Broad: men and women over 40, general "wellness" (brain fog, energy, digestion, inflammation).
  • Through targeting and videos: men over 50 with an enlarged prostate / on Flomax (otherwise they wouldn't rank #1 on these searches).
  • Grandparents (the granddaughter and pinworms story): 55-70 target who share on Facebook.
  • US Spanish speakers (ads in Spanish).

Promises

  • "Brain fog lifts", energy, digestion, lower inflammation; "dissolves parasite shells".
  • For the prostate (in the videos): less inflammation, fewer night trips.
  • Purity: cold-pressed, third-party tested, "zero unnecessary" additives.

Offers and landing pages

  • purelynutrient.com/pages/ethiopian-black-seed-oil (46 ads): single long landing page, "listicle" style.
  • purelynutrient.com/pages/pp-48 (11 ads): page variant (test).
  • 5 Facebook pages: "Purely Nutrient Black Seed", "Purely-Nutrient", "The Ethiopian Journal", "Top 10 Holistic Tips", "The Wellness Journal": "media" pages (journal, top 10) so the ad looks like an article.

Formats

  • 96% video (55 out of 57): the same copy, dozens of different videos (the opposite of Elivora). They test video creatives at scale with fixed copy.
  • Short copy, no long story: the video does the work.
  • The "Top 10 Holistic Tips" page = their best-ranking page (#1 on "enlarged prostate" and "Flomax").

What the videos say (6 transcribed out of 55): THIS is where the prostate angle is

  • "This is a swollen prostate" (Sept 16, 2026, 3 variants, 5,000-char script): repeated three times at the open, then "three warning signs": weak stream ("a fist around a garden hose"), night trips, leaking after pulling your underwear back on. Mechanism sold: "chronic inflammation… like cement, hardened waste, toxins, and hormonal byproducts compounding inside the tissue year after year". Threat: "a scope up your urethra… surgery with a 75% chance of permanent side effects".
  • "This is a dead prostate" (3 variants): "the best thing to fix it is not saw palmetto, pumpkin seeds, or the medication your urologist keeps pushing": they attack pumpkin seed and saw palmetto directly (so Everly, Elivora and Uromend) to sell black seed.
  • The 72-hour journey (2 videos, prostate and gut): "You accidentally swallow a softgel of Ethiopian black seed oil. It can still affect your prostate for the next 72 hours… By hour 12, the thymoquinone passes directly through the cell membranes of your prostate tissue… By hour 24… the tissue begins to soften… By hour 48…". A "what happens in your body hour by hour" format, heavily watched.
  • Sex + Flomax (3 variants): "This is how a 42-year-old man gets his big loads back without ever touching another Flomax refill… The dry orgasms. The cloudy dribble after… every Flomax refill just relaxed the pipe while the swelling sat there getting worse". Same "3 days / day 10 / 3 weeks" structure as Noverly (same writer or same template).
  • Parasites / candida (women): "Clean your vagina in just one night… there's something alive inside you… parasites build a thick protective shield called biofilm. Wormwood bounces right off it". The word biofilm is everywhere: it's their signature mechanism ("dissolves that biofilm").
  • Proof: "tested at 4.64% thymoquinone. Nine times stronger"; "Highland farms at 8,000 feet".
  • The two "prostate" videos are the ones with 3 variants each: they are their best. Downloadable from the file (local copy kept).

Hooks, awareness level, personas, enemies, narrative (indicative figures from 10/17; the charts below are recalculated at each snapshot)

  • #1 copy hook: the catalog (93%: the same copy "Purely Nutrient Ethiopian Black Seed Oil is one of nature's most potent…"): the real hook is in the video: "This is a swollen prostate" (×3), "This is a dead prostate" (×3), "You accidentally swallow a softgel… 72 hours", "Clean your vagina in just one night".
  • Awareness level: the copy speaks to the product aware (91%: brand name in the first line); the videos speak to the unaware ("something is inside you: parasites, hardened waste") and to the problem aware (prostate).
  • Persona (from the transcribed videos): man 50+ prostate (the 2 best videos), woman 40+ (candida, parasites), grandparents (pinworms), Spanish speakers.
  • Enemy: parasites / biofilm / hardened waste (their signature mechanism), other supplements ("not saw palmetto, pumpkin seeds"), Flomax ("every Flomax refill just relaxed the pipe").
  • Narrative: catalog (copy) + timeline mechanism in video (72 h, day 3/10, 3 weeks) + shock image repeated three times.

What it means for Uromend

  • Black seed is arriving in the prostate space (Sabel Life too): a trendy ingredient; Uromend doesn't have it. No need to add it, but prepare the "what about black seed oil?" question in ads/FAQ.
  • Their method (fixed copy + 50 videos) is the opposite of Everly/Elivora (image + 50 copies). Uromend does little of both. The Purely method is the most accessible for Saad (video editing): keep a copy that works and produce 5 videos per week.
  • Ranking #1 on "enlarged prostate" in one month with a non-prostate product shows the spot is won with volume and targeting, not relevance: Uromend can take it back with 30-50 videos on the same angle.
  • The "journal / top 10" pages (disguised media) are a clean idea to reuse: a "Men's Night Guide" or "Prostate Health Daily" page publishing tips and ads.
  • To watch: 0 → 365 in a month; if the next count shows 600+, they found a winning video: transcribe and analyze it first.

Everyone Planning to Try Purely Nutrient Needs to Know These 6 Unexpected Side Effects
Purely Nutrient is Ethiopian black seed oil at 4.64% thymoquinone, which is roughly 9 times the strength of what's sold on a shelf. Two softgels before bed. But the effects most women write in about aren't the ones they bought it for, and a couple of them genuinely surprised us. So here they are.
SIDE EFFECT 1: You stop planning your day around your stomach
Remember eating dinner at 4:30 so you'd be past the worst of it before anyone saw you? Changing out of the jeans the second you got home? Holding your cardigan closed in photos?
Most women buy this for the bloating. What they don't expect is how much of their life was quietly organised around it.
"I wore the same pants at 8pm that I put on at 8 in the morning. First time in four years."
SIDE EFFECT 2: The sugar cravings stop
This is the one nobody sees coming.
If something is living in your gut, it feeds before you do, and it has a preference. That 11pm pull toward something sweet that never made sense and never matched your willpower? It wasn't a discipline problem.
"I went past the biscuit aisle and just genuinely did not want any. I stood there for a second because it was so strange."
SIDE EFFECT 3: You sleep through the night
The 3am wake up where nothing's wrong and you're just awake. Most women have had it so long they file it under being over 50.
"I woke up at 4 and the room was quiet and I laid there trying to work out what was different."
SIDE EFFECT 4: Your afternoons come back
Not energy in the supplement-ad sense. Just the 2 o'clock hole closing up. The one where you've had 7 hours and you're still hunting for a reason to sit down.
"My husband said I'm laughing more. I think he's right."
SIDE EFFECT 5: Less puffiness in the face
Nobody buys black seed oil for their face. But the morning puffiness around the eyes and jaw is the thing friends tend to comment on first, usually before you've told anyone you're taking anything.
"A woman at work asked if I'd been away somewhere."
SIDE EFFECT 6: You stop apologising for your body
This is the one that actually matters.
When you've spent years hiding your stomach from your own husband, the physical thing fixing itself is only half of it. The other half is not flinching.
"He put his hand on my stomach in the kitchen, completely absentmindedly, and I didn't move it."
WHY THIS WORKS WHEN THE OTHER THINGS DIDN'T
You've almost certainly tried some of these:
❌ Cleanses. They work for about two weeks, then everything comes back and you decide you did it wrong. You didn't. A cleanse kills the grown ones and never touches the eggs.
❌ Probiotics. Adding good bacteria doesn't remove something that's already built a coating around itself in there.
❌ Elimination diets. Cutting out bread, dairy, gluten and onions one at a time doesn't remove what's already living there. That's why nothing ever lined up and some days a salad set it off and some days a pizza didn't.
❌ Black seed oil from a shelf. About half a percent thymoquinone. It isn't getting through anything.
THE PART NOBODY EXPLAINS
They don't sit out in the open. Whatever's down there builds a film around itself, and that's why your immune system never deals with it. Your body isn't ignoring the problem. It can't find the problem. It's also why nothing ever shows up on a test, because nobody is looking behind the film.
And it's exactly why every cleanse dies at two weeks. The eggs sit behind that coating untouched, hatch about two weeks later, and the whole thing rebuilds.
✔️ At 4.64% thymoquinone it dissolves the coating ✔️ Then it clears the grown ones and the eggs together ✔️ So there's nothing left in there waiting to hatch
That's the whole difference, and it's the reason the concentration matters more than anything else on the label.
Two softgels before bed.

Everyone Planning to Try Purely Nutrient Needs to Know These 6 Unexpected Side Effects
Purely Nutrient is Ethiopian black seed oil at 4.64% thymoquinone, which is roughly 9 times the strength of what's sold on a shelf. Two softgels before bed. But the effects most women write in about aren't the ones they bought it for, and a couple of them genuinely surprised us. So here they are.
SIDE EFFECT 1: You stop planning your day around your stomach
Remember eating dinner at 4:30 so you'd be past the worst of it before anyone saw you? Changing out of the jeans the second you got home? Holding your cardigan closed in photos?
Most women buy this for the bloating. What they don't expect is how much of their life was quietly organised around it.
"I wore the same pants at 8pm that I put on at 8 in the morning. First time in four years."
SIDE EFFECT 2: The sugar cravings stop
This is the one nobody sees coming.
If something is living in your gut, it feeds before you do, and it has a preference. That 11pm pull toward something sweet that never made sense and never matched your willpower? It wasn't a discipline problem.
"I went past the biscuit aisle and just genuinely did not want any. I stood there for a second because it was so strange."
SIDE EFFECT 3: You sleep through the night
The 3am wake up where nothing's wrong and you're just awake. Most women have had it so long they file it under being over 50.
"I woke up at 4 and the room was quiet and I laid there trying to work out what was different."
SIDE EFFECT 4: Your afternoons come back
Not energy in the supplement-ad sense. Just the 2 o'clock hole closing up. The one where you've had 7 hours and you're still hunting for a reason to sit down.
"My husband said I'm laughing more. I think he's right."
SIDE EFFECT 5: Less puffiness in the face
Nobody buys black seed oil for their face. But the morning puffiness around the eyes and jaw is the thing friends tend to comment on first, usually before you've told anyone you're taking anything.
"A woman at work asked if I'd been away somewhere."
SIDE EFFECT 6: You stop apologising for your body
This is the one that actually matters.
When you've spent years hiding your stomach from your own husband, the physical thing fixing itself is only half of it. The other half is not flinching.
"He put his hand on my stomach in the kitchen, completely absentmindedly, and I didn't move it."
WHY THIS WORKS WHEN THE OTHER THINGS DIDN'T
You've almost certainly tried some of these:
❌ Cleanses. They work for about two weeks, then everything comes back and you decide you did it wrong. You didn't. A cleanse kills the grown ones and never touches the eggs.
❌ Probiotics. Adding good bacteria doesn't remove something that's already built a coating around itself in there.
❌ Elimination diets. Cutting out bread, dairy, gluten and onions one at a time doesn't remove what's already living there. That's why nothing ever lined up and some days a salad set it off and some days a pizza didn't.
❌ Black seed oil from a shelf. About half a percent thymoquinone. It isn't getting through anything.
THE PART NOBODY EXPLAINS
They don't sit out in the open. Whatever's down there builds a film around itself, and that's why your immune system never deals with it. Your body isn't ignoring the problem. It can't find the problem. It's also why nothing ever shows up on a test, because nobody is looking behind the film.
And it's exactly why every cleanse dies at two weeks. The eggs sit behind that coating untouched, hatch about two weeks later, and the whole thing rebuilds.
✔️ At 4.64% thymoquinone it dissolves the coating ✔️ Then it clears the grown ones and the eggs together ✔️ So there's nothing left in there waiting to hatch
That's the whole difference, and it's the reason the concentration matters more than anything else on the label.
Two softgels before bed.

I did not believe him.

I have not spoken to him in 15 years.
—
My name is Carol.
I am 46.
For 15 years I have carried a private resentment toward Andrew that I have rarely talked about out loud.
It sat in my chest every time I had an outbreak.
Every time I had to disclose to a new partner.
Every time I took a Valtrex.
Every time I saw a man on Hinge with a name like Andrew or a face like his.
15 years of quietly blaming a specific person for a specific moment that ruined a specific stretch of my life.
I had a whole story about him.
I had told it to myself so many times it had become memory.
—
Last month I was scrolling at midnight and a video came up of a parasitologist showing a slide of something called Clonorchis sinensis.
A liver fluke.
She said it gets into the body through raw fish.
Sushi specifically.
She said it can sit in the liver and bile duct for years.
Then she said the sentence that stopped me.
She said: liver flukes are linked to herpes.
I sat up.
I rewound it.
I listened again.
She explained that herpes is not classified the way most people think.
That in some medical literature it is categorized as an obligate intracellular parasite.
That the same parasite ecology you get from contaminated food can sit dormant in your nervous system for years before it manifests.
That the timeline between exposure and diagnosis can be anywhere from months to over a decade.
I sat in my bed and I started doing math.
—
I lived in San Francisco from 2003 to 2007.
I ate sushi probably twice a week for 4 years.
I worked across the street from a place that I now know, because I checked their Yelp from that era, had multiple complaints about raw fish quality.
Andrew and I started dating in March of 2008.
I was diagnosed in February of 2009.
I had spent 15 years certain that the 11 months between those two dates contained the source of my diagnosis.
I had never once considered the 4 years before I met him.
4 years of sushi twice a week.
4 years of an exposure I had filed under food I ate and never thought about again.
I sat there at midnight doing math I should have done in 2009 and never did, because nobody had ever told me to.
—
What that parasitologist was talking about:
Herpes is classified in some medical literature as an obligate intracellular parasite.
Not just a virus.
A parasite.
The organism hides in your nerve tissue between outbreaks.
Dormant.
Producing eggs on its own.
Up to 26,000 a day.
And the reason nothing has ever reached it is that it wraps itself in a slime shield called biofilm.
Antivirals work on the bloodstream.
They cannot get through the biofilm, and they cannot reach the dormant organism buried in nerve tissue.
That is why the outbreaks keep coming.
That is why managing is forever.
There is exactly one natural compound that can reach it.
Thymoquinone.
The active compound in black seed oil.
It is lipophilic, which means it does not push against the biofilm from the outside like everything else.
It dissolves the shield from the inside out, reaches the nerve tissue nothing else could, and destroys the parasite at every stage.
The adults.
The larvae.
And the eggs, so they cannot hatch two weeks later and start the cycle over.
That last part is the reason most cleanses fail at week 3.
But here is what almost no one tells you.
Most black seed oil does nothing.
The cheap kind from Egypt or India sits at less than 1% thymoquinone, far too weak to break biofilm.
The only concentration strong enough is 4.64%, and it only comes from black seed grown in the Ethiopian highlands at 8,000 feet.
The only brand sourcing it directly from those farms is Purely Nutrient.

Stalin's Doctors Put Leeches Behind His Ears To Bring His Blood Pressure Down. It Was 190/110 When They Got To Him, And This Was 1953. The President Who Sat Next To Him At Yalta Had His Blood Pressure Written Down For 10 Years Before It Hit 300 Over 190.
I taught American history at the high school for 33 years, and every spring I put the same picture from Yalta up on the overhead projector, Roosevelt and Stalin sitting there side by side.
And every year I said the same thing, look at Roosevelt, gray as a sidewalk, he's dead in 2 months. Grown men still yell it at me in the grocery store.
I'm 66 and retired, and once a month I do a history talk at our library on a Saturday morning. Yalta is my old faithful.
The week all this happened I had my checkup on the Tuesday. My numbers had been creeping up for years, the top one was in the 120s when I retired and its gone up a couple points every year since, and every year my doc said watch the salt. I took the shaker off the table and figured that was that. Never felt a thing, I still split our own firewood. This time it was 146 on top and she put her pen down, which she doesn't usually do.
She wants readings at home for 2 weeks before anybody says the word pill, because a lot of people read higher in the office. And walk more and cut the salt and come back.
Wednesday I went looking for a better copy of that picture and ended up in a paper out of a medical school in Albania from a few years ago about the health of the big 3 at Yalta. Halfway down there's a little table.
FDR's blood pressure, by year.
1935, 136 over 78. 1937, 162 over 98. 1941, 188 over 105. 1944, 226 over 118.
33 years I taught this man and never knew anybody wrote his blood pressure down, every number higher than the one before.
Then April 12, 1945, Warm Springs, Georgia. He's sitting for a portrait and he says "I have a terrific headache" and goes down, and his heart doctor takes his pressure and it's 300 over 190. He was gone a few hours later, 63 years old.
The next day one of the papers had his doctor saying it "came out of clear sky."
I read that out loud to Margie and she said out of a clear sky?? with 10 years of his numbers written down?
The paper gets into that. Back then most doctors figured high pressure was the body doing its job, pushing blood through hardened arteries, and the big heart textbook of the time said it might be something that "should not be tampered with." So some of his doctors probably just didn't think those numbers were as bad as they were.
Then Stalin, which I knew would be the hit of the talk. In 1953 when his doctors finally got to him after his stroke he was 190 over 110, and to try and bring it down they put leeches behind his ears. Leeches. My dad bought a brand new Buick in 1953.
I wrote my Tuesday number in pencil in the margin and it goes right between his first 2. He smoked like a chimney and ran a war from a wheelchair, so I'm not making it into anything, I just sat at the kitchen table with it awhile.
Saturday I did the talk. The 5 readings and it got real quiet. Then the leeches and the whole room went EWWW like a bunch of 10th graders.
Then questions. Clyde, Margie's sister's husband, sits in the front row every month with his arms folded to "keep me honest," and he says it loud enough for the back row.
"Tell em yours, Gil."
Margie had told Nadine on the phone. Nadine tells Clyde everything.
I said Clyde, this is about Yalta. And he turns around in his chair and says "He's at 146, folks, somebody call the bait shop and see if they got leeches."
They laughed. The librarian laughed and tried not to. The rest of the questions were about their own blood pressure, one guy asking about his 152 while I'm up there with a laser pointer going sir, I teach history.
Sunday we go to Nadine's for dinner and there's a little baggie of gummy worms by my plate. Clyde never said a word about it, just kept looking at the baggie and then at me, all through the pot roast.

Doctors Used To Put Live Leeches On People To Let Out Blood They Figured Was Bad, Or Just Too Much Of It. At One Point France Alone Went Through 50 To 100 Million Leeches A Year. I Paid $40 At An Estate Sale For One Of The Jars They Kept Them In, And Now It Sits On My Dresser Full Of My Own Blood Pressure Numbers.
Little paper price tags, the kind with the string, same ones I've hung on everything I've sold for 30 some years. Every morning I write the number off the cuff on one and drop it in. Dot says it's the ugliest thing in the house.
I'm 63, I'm a picker. Estate sales, farm auctions, barns, I've got a booth at the antique mall by the interstate. Basically I buy dead people's stuff, Dot hates when I put it like that.
The jar came out of Bernice's cellar, her estate sale south of town. She's selling out and moving to Tulsa by her son, and her great grandpa ran the drugstore here back in the 1800s.
Gus called it off the back of a hay wagon like he's called about every sale in this county since I was in my 20s.
Wendell and me had just carried a walnut dresser up those cellar stairs, so I'm standing there red in the face and sweated through my shirt when Gus holds up this glass jar about the size of a big pickle jar, tin lid punched full of holes.
"Leech jar folks, off the counter of the old drugstore. Holes are so they could breathe."
Then he looks right at me.
"Monty you oughta bid on this one. You look like you could stand to let a pint out."
The whole yard laughed. The church ladies at the pie table, Bernice, guys I've bid against my whole life. I said 40 dollars and nobody went against me, I think they were still laughing, and Gus says "SOLD to the Doc."
So that's my name now. Every Saturday Gus spots me in the crowd and says it on the mic, "Doc's here, everybody hang onto your necks," and they laugh every time like it's new. And I'm at his sales every weekend, that's where the stuff is.
I research everything I buy, you can't price what you don't understand, and this one got wierd fast.
There's a whole paper in a medical history journal on the leech trade back then. France went so crazy for them they used up their own and about wiped out Spain's too. Drugstores kept them in water in jars like mine. They'd put them on you for headaches, fevers, a bad stomach, about anything, the idea being you had bad blood in you, or too much of it, and you let some out.
And a history piece in one of the big blood pressure journals said one of the early things anybody tried for pressure running high was leeches, and some old Chinese medical book from thousands of years back already said salt had something to do with it. Dot just looked at me over her glasses.
The part nobody believes is they still use them. The FDA cleared leeches as a medical device in 2004. When a surgeon sews a finger or an ear back on and the blood gets in but can't get back out, they can put a leech on it to keep it draining. I printed that for Gus and he said "well then you're all set, Doc."
Oh and I forgot to mention, a few weeks after I bought the jar I had my checkup.
My top number's been creeping up for years, it used to start with a 12, and every year my doctor said watch the salt and every year I said yep. This time the nurse got 148. I never felt one thing. I told her my face gets red hauling furniture and she said that's the furniture, high blood pressure usually doesn't have any symptoms.
She didn't want to jump to a pill. She wanted me, well she wanted a lot of things, checking it at home every morning, walking, cutting the salt, taking some of the gut off, and come back in 3 months.
I got a cuff on the way home and set it on the dresser by the jar, and the first morning I had nothing to write on but the tags in my shirt pocket. The first couple weeks were all 140 something.
Dot went through my truck. I've kept a salt shaker in the console forever for the boiled eggs at the gas station. She dropped it in the jar on top of the tags and its still in there.

That White Frayed Stuff On The Screen Is The Inside Of A Worn Out Knee. I Was Awake And Watched Them Clean Mine Out On A Screen Just Like This. Then I Found The Study Where Surgeons Faked It On A Third Of The Patients, Never Went Inside The Knee, And For 2 Years The Real Surgery Did No Better.
I'm 64. I was a plumber for 38 years, and if you know that trade you already know where this is going. Half of it is on your knees on somebody's bathroom tile and the other half is on your back under a sink. My right knee took most of it.
The scope was my brother in law Ted's idea.
Ted is Connie's older brother. Sold insurance his whole life and knows a little about everything, just ask him. Thanksgiving 2010 I got down on the floor at their house to help a nephew with a train set and couldn't get back up, had to roll over and push off the couch, and Ted watched from his recliner and said loud enough for the kitchen, "Phil, you get up like my grandmother. Go see my guy. Best thing I ever did, I was back on the golf course in 2 weeks."
So I went. The surgeon looked at the X ray and said arthritis, and that he could go in and clean it out, trim the rough stuff and wash out the junk, buy me some years. They did mine with a spinal so I was awake and could watch it on a TV screen next to the table. The inside of my own knee. All this white frayed stuff floating around like crab meat and him going at it with a little shaver. I told everybody about that TV for a month.
3 little cuts, 3 weeks off work, and when you're self employed nobody pays you for those 3 weeks.
It helped some, maybe, for a while. By that fall I was back to sitting on the tailgate to strap my knee pads on and back to the Aleve with breakfast.
But Ted asked at every holiday. "How's the knee? Told ya my guy was good." And I'd paid all that and I was NOT going to give Ted the satisfaction, so I said good as new. For years. Connie knew better and kept her mouth shut, bless her.
Then Ted and Judy's 40th anniversary party at the Elks. The DJ played the chicken dance because of course he did, Judy grabbed me, and on about the third squat my right knee just went. Sideways. Next thing I'm flat on my back on the dance floor in my good pants with the whole hall looking at me.
And Ted gets on the DJ's microphone. "Phil, I got you the best knee man in the state and you still can't do the chicken dance."
Everybody laughed. Connie and their oldest boy had to get me up. I laughed too, what else are you gonna do, and told everybody I must of landed wrong.
Last year I was doing PT for that knee, griping to the PT, a kid half my age, that I already had it cleaned out in 2011 for all the good it did. He kind of stopped and said "you know about the fake surgery study, right?"
I said what fake surgery study.
I went home and made Connie pull it up on the computer with me because I didn't believe him. New England Journal of Medicine, 2002, some doctors down in Houston. They took 180 people with arthritis in their knees and split them 3 ways without telling them which one they got. A third got cleaned out like me, a third just got washed out, and the last third got the fake one, cuts in the skin, the whole surgery acted out, and the camera never went in their knee. Even the people checking on them afterward didn't know who had what.
They followed them 2 years. At no point did either real surgery group have less pain or get around any better than the fake group, I read that line about 4 times. And from what I read, when they asked the fake group later, most of them figured they'd had the real thing.
That was 2002. And mine was 2011, I sat there and counted it out on my fingers at the kitchen table like a kid.
I'm not saying my surgeon did anything wrong. I never asked him one question about it, I just went because Ted said.

His name was Andrew.
We dated for 9 months in 2008.
He was the only person I had been with in the year leading up to my diagnosis.
When my test came back positive in 2009 I knew immediately who had given it to me.
I called him.
He denied it.
He said he had been tested, he was clean, it must have been someone before him.
I did not believe him.
I told him to never contact me again.
I have not spoken to him in 15 years.
—
My name is Carol.
I am 46.
For 15 years I have carried a private resentment toward Andrew that I have rarely talked about out loud.
It sat in my chest every time I had an outbreak.
Every time I had to disclose to a new partner.
Every time I took a Valtrex.
Every time I saw a man on Hinge with a name like Andrew or a face like his.
15 years of quietly blaming a specific person for a specific moment that ruined a specific stretch of my life.
I had a whole story about him.
I had told it to myself so many times it had become memory.
—
Last month I was scrolling at midnight and a video came up of a parasitologist showing a slide of something called Clonorchis sinensis.
A liver fluke.
She said it gets into the body through raw fish.
Sushi specifically.
She said it can sit in the liver and bile duct for years.
Then she said the sentence that stopped me.
She said: liver flukes are linked to herpes.
I sat up.
I rewound it.
I listened again.
She explained that herpes is not classified the way most people think.
That in some medical literature it is categorized as an obligate intracellular parasite.
That the same parasite ecology you get from contaminated food can sit dormant in your nervous system for years before it manifests.
That the timeline between exposure and diagnosis can be anywhere from months to over a decade.
I sat in my bed and I started doing math.
—
I lived in San Francisco from 2003 to 2007.
I ate sushi probably twice a week for 4 years.
I worked across the street from a place that I now know, because I checked their Yelp from that era, had multiple complaints about raw fish quality.
Andrew and I started dating in March of 2008.
I was diagnosed in February of 2009.
I had spent 15 years certain that the 11 months between those two dates contained the source of my diagnosis.
I had never once considered the 4 years before I met him.
4 years of sushi twice a week.
4 years of an exposure I had filed under food I ate and never thought about again.
I sat there at midnight doing math I should have done in 2009 and never did, because nobody had ever told me to.
—
What that parasitologist was talking about:
Herpes is classified in some medical literature as an obligate intracellular parasite.
Not just a virus.
A parasite.
The organism hides in your nerve tissue between outbreaks.
Dormant.
Producing eggs on its own.
Up to 26,000 a day.
And the reason nothing has ever reached it is that it wraps itself in a slime shield called biofilm.
Antivirals work on the bloodstream.
They cannot get through the biofilm, and they cannot reach the dormant organism buried in nerve tissue.
That is why the outbreaks keep coming.
That is why managing is forever.
There is exactly one natural compound that can reach it.
Thymoquinone.
The active compound in black seed oil.
It is lipophilic, which means it does not push against the biofilm from the outside like everything else.
It dissolves the shield from the inside out, reaches the nerve tissue nothing else could, and destroys the parasite at every stage.
The adults.
The larvae.
And the eggs, so they cannot hatch two weeks later and start the cycle over.
That last part is the reason most cleanses fail at week 3.
But here is what almost no one tells you.
Most black seed oil does nothing.
The cheap kind from Egypt or India sits at less than 1% thymoquinone, far too weak to break biofilm.
The only concentration strong enough is 4.64%, and it only comes from black seed grown in the Ethiopian highlands at 8,000 feet.
The only brand sourcing it directly from those farms is Purely Nutrient.

My Doctor Clipped Both My Knee X-Rays Up On His Lightbox, Put His Pen On The Left One And Said Bone On Bone, Wear And Tear. I Had To Tell Him That's Not The One That Hurts. The One That Hurts Looks Almost Normal.
I've laid carpet 34 years, I'm 61. If you don't know the trade there's a tool called a knee kicker, you hook it in the carpet and bang the pad with your knee to stretch it to the wall, all day long, and I kick with my left. Always have. So when a knee started hurting a couple years back I figured ok, here's the bill.
Only it was the right one.
Getting up off the floor was the worst of it, and getting in the truck I'd grab my jeans above the knee and lift that leg in with my hand.
My brother in law Stan is my partner. Stan does the selling since he got his knee replaced, and since then Stan knows everything there is about knees. For about a year his position was quit whining and go get it scoped.
So Carla made the appointment. The bone doctor is about my age and still has a lightbox on the wall. They X-rayed both knees standing up and he clipped them side by side and put his pen right on the left one.
Well there it is, he says, that's bone on bone, that's your wear and tear right there.

He looked at me and back at the films a while. The right one looks pretty good actually, he says, a little narrowing, nothing that'd explain alot, could be something that doesn't show up on an X-ray. I asked the desk for copies, I think to show Stan. The girl said nobody asks for film anymore but she found me the big envelope, and a CD too, which I have nothing to put in.
